To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the docking of highly flexible molecules is possible by a multistep docking procedure and that this approach allows the accurate prediction (within a root mean square deviation of 0.5 A) of the ligand poses and the ligand binding free energies (within a root-mean-squared deviation of 2.2 kcal/mol) for a number of protein-ligand systems that are known to be challenging for other docking programs.
the docking of flexible ligands into protein binding sites can be improved significantly by using a multistep procedure that restricts the rotational space during the conformational sampling.
the multistep docking procedure is able to predict ligand poses and binding affinities with high accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a docking method for flexible ligands that is able to predict protein-ligand complex structures with a high accuracy.

the development and evaluation of a multistep docking procedure that allows the accurate and reliable prediction of the orientation, conformation, and binding affinity of ligands in their protein binding site, especially in the case of highly flexible ligands.
the development of an improved docking procedure that is able to predict the correct orientation and conformation for ligands with high rotational freedom in a protein binding pocket.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the procedure is able to provide a good starting point for the subsequent refinement of the ligand conformation and orientation in the binding site.
the method described here is capable of producing accurate ligand poses in protein binding sites and is a valuable addition to existing methods for molecular docking.
the method is able to predict the correct orientation of a ligand in the active site of a protein with a high degree (80%) of accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the procedure is able to accurately predict the binding modes and poses of a wide range of flexible ligands, including those with extended molecular structures.
our method is able to predict the ligand poses with an accuracy comparable to the crystallographic data.
the procedure is able to predict protein-ligand complex geometries with high accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a multistep docking procedure is an effective way to overcome the limitations of docking programs in the presence of highly flexible ligands.

, by combining the local docking procedure with the QXP scoring function, the prediction accuracy of the ligand pose can be increased to a level where the docking program can be applied to a broad range of ligands and protein-ligand systems.

, in order to obtain accurate results for the prediction of protein-ligand complex structures, it is necessary to perform docking calculations with a high number of poses, which is possible only with a multistep procedure.
